items.title: Lesson Podcast
items.description: Audio guide to primacy and recency effects, the serial position curve, and Murdock's word-list study.

items.title: All in the Mind — BBC Radio 4
items.description: Radio 4 programme on memory research — episodes on recall and forgetting are directly relevant to why we remember beginnings and endings of lists.

items.title: Murdock's Serial Position Curve Study
items.description: Focused revision video explaining Murdock's 1962 free-recall study, the U-shaped curve and what primacy and recency tell us about STM and LTM.

items.title: Memory 2 — AQA GCSE Psychology
items.description: AQA-specific revision video covering serial position, the primacy/recency effects and their implications for memory models.

items.title: Remembering and Forgetting: Crash Course Psychology #14
items.description: Explains encoding failures, retrieval cues and why certain items in a list are more memorable — extends the serial position discussion.

items.title: Memento
items.description: Story told in reverse order that dramatises how memory retrieval depends on cues — a creative way to think about primacy and encoding failure.

items.title: Simply Psychology — Serial Position Effect
items.description: Explains the primacy and recency effects, the serial position curve and the evidence linking them to STM/LTM separation.

items.title: AQA GCSE Psychology 8182 — Specification
items.description: Official AQA spec listing the Murdock study content and the assessment objectives for the memory unit.
